brief: Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's midterms, initially easing Iran-tension fears, but equities reversed hard Thursday on AI-regulation worries plus weak semiconductor guidance: Nasdaq 100 fell 6.4% and semiconductors over 12%, both worst since March 2020, wiping out $2.8 trillion in a single day, the largest on record. The selloff ranks as the 5th-largest VIX spike ever, put/call ratios hit the most bearish since April 2025, and retail turned net seller for only the second time this year. Asian AI-linked markets lost roughly $7 trillion, led by South Korea's Kospi death cross. Stocks partially recovered Friday as October payrolls beat sharply (165K vs 70K est), reviving December Fed hike odds to about 20bps; yields had fallen on the Democratic sweep (less fiscal expansion expected) before hawkish data tempered that rally. Separately, a Democratic Texas governor win raised doubt the state's data-center construction moratorium lifts soon, and Microsoft is unwinding its Oracle AI cloud rental deal even as Anthropic's revenue and IPO scale keep growing.
